description:
VMImage — a cluster-scoped, backend-agnostic catalog entry for a bootable
guest image.

A VMImage names an operating system (family / distribution / version /
architecture) once, then lists — per provider class — where that image
actually lives on each backend (`spec.sources`). A VirtualMachine
references a VMImage by name (`spec.imageRef`); the scheduler and the
chosen provider resolve it to a concrete template / backing file / import
URL at provisioning time.

# Why create one

- **One name, many backends.** "ubuntu-22.04" can map to a vSphere
  template, a Proxmox template VMID, and a libvirt qcow2 — users reference
  a single VMImage regardless of where the VM lands.
- **Explicit, auditable image sourcing.** Sources (and optional checksums)
  are declared, not auto-discovered, so what actually boots is reviewable.
- **Readiness gating.** The image controller records per-Provider
  readiness in `status`; the scheduler refuses to place a VM until the
  image is confirmed available (or importable) on a candidate Provider.

Cluster-scoped: a VMImage is shared by VirtualMachines in any namespace.

apiVersion.description: APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.

kind.description: Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.

spec.description:
VMImage — a cluster-scoped, backend-agnostic catalog entry for a bootable
guest image.

# Why create one

- **Explicit, auditable image sourcing.** Sources (and optional checksums)

architecture.description:
Guest CPU architecture. Failure domains whose hosts cannot run this
architecture are filtered out by the scheduler.

cloudConfigs.description:
Layered cloud-configs baked into the built artifact for `Url`-kind
sources (ADR-0037). `banlieue-imagebuilder` fetches each referenced
Secret in list order, deep-merges their YAML content (maps deep-merge,
lists concatenate, type-mismatch errors), SSA-applies a single merged
Secret (`<vmimage-name>-cloud-config-merged`), and passes *that* to
the kairos-operator `OSArtifact` as `cloudConfigRef`
(`auroraboot build-iso --cloud-config`). Empty list = no cloud-config.
Index 0 is the base; each subsequent entry layers on top.
SecretRef-first; see `CloudConfigSource` and ADR-0020.
Ignored for non-`Url` sources.

items.description:
Source of a default cloud-config baked into a built image artifact.

Mirrors `CABundleSource`'s value-or-source shape, but is **secretRef-first**
(ADR-0020): only `secret_ref` is implemented today, because kairos-operator's
`OSArtifact.spec.cloudConfigRef` is itself Secret-only and
`banlieue-imagebuilder` passes this Secret straight through. The `inline` and
`config_map_ref` variants are reserved for a later change (they will resolve
by materialising an imagebuilder-owned derived Secret); adding them is an
additive, non-breaking CRD change.

secretRef.description:
Key in a Secret in the imagebuild namespace holding the cloud-config
YAML (key defaults to `DEFAULT_CLOUD_CONFIG_KEY`).

key.description: Key within the object's `data`. Defaults are caller-defined.

name.description: Name of the ConfigMap / Secret in the referrer's namespace.

firstBootSealing.description:
Declares that every clone of this image seals the listed partitions
to its own vTPM on its first boot (ADR-0088), which is what lets a
`VMClass` with `tpmEnabled: true` use an `Immediate` (pre-installed)
image. Without it that pairing is refused, because the template was
installed before any per-VM vTPM existed (ADR-0048).

For a `Url` source `banlieue-imagebuilder` writes the sealing policy
into the built image itself (`status.firstBootSealing: Built`); for a
`Template` or `BackingFile` source the image must already carry it, and
this field is an operator assertion (`Asserted`). Either way every
clone's `GuestReady` waits for the guest to report each listed
partition sealed. Needs a source image on Kairos v4.4.0 or later.
Honoured unless `banlieue-controller` runs with
`--enable-first-boot-sealing=false`, which refuses a `VirtualMachine`
of this image (`FirstBootSealingDisabled`). Not combinable with
`trustedBoot`.

partitions.description:
Kairos partition labels to seal on first boot. Defaults to
`[COS_PERSISTENT]`. `COS_OEM`, `COS_STATE`, `COS_RECOVERY` and
`COS_GRUB` are refused at admission, mirroring Kairos's own refusal.

timeoutSeconds.description:
Seconds from the machine's power-on (its infrastructure `Ready`
transition) within which the guest must report every listed partition
sealed; after that `GuestReady` is `False` with reason
`FirstBootSealingTimeout`. A clone that cannot seal halts in its
initramfs and never reports anything, so this is how it is noticed.

guestAgent.description:
Guest agent contract this image is built to support; determines how
`VirtualMachine.spec.userData` is delivered.

isoOverlay.description:
Additional files overlaid onto a built ISO for `Url`-kind vSphere
sources (e.g. a hand-verified `grub.cfg`). Resolved by
`banlieue-imagebuilder` into the kairos-operator `OSArtifact`'s
`spec.volumes[]` + `spec.artifacts.overlayISOVolume` — the same
`auroraboot build-iso --overlay-iso` mechanism a hand-run ISO-build
pipeline would use. See `IsoOverlaySource` and ADR-0022. Ignored for
`cloudImage`-kind builds and non-`Url` sources.

files.description:
Explicit key -> ISO-relative-path mapping. At least one entry expected;
an empty list is accepted but wires nothing into the `OSArtifact`.

items.description:
One overlay file: a key within `IsoOverlaySource::secret_ref` mapped to
a destination path relative to the built ISO's root.

key.description: Key within the overlay Secret holding this file's content.

path.description: Destination path, relative to the ISO root (e.g. `boot/grub2/grub.cfg`).

secretRef.description: Secret in the imagebuild namespace holding the overlay file contents.

osDistribution.description:
Free-form distribution string. Examples: ubuntu, rhel, debian,
fedora-coreos, windows-server.

osFamily.description:
Broad operating-system family. Coarser than `osDistribution`; lets
providers apply high-level guest handling.

prelay.description:
Pre-lay the built image (ADR-0113): `banlieue-imagebuilder` boots the
raw `cloudImage` once, at build time, through the Kairos recovery
reset every clone would otherwise run on its first boot, so each
clone boots straight into the installed system. Only for a `Url`
source built as a `cloudImage`; an `iso` build is refused
(`PrelayNeedsCloudImage`). The pre-lay Job runs the published
`banlieue-prelay` image (`banlieue-imagebuilder --prelay-image`) and
needs `/dev/kvm` on the build node. The published artifact is the pre-laid file, with a
checksum the builder computed after verifying the built file against
the source's `checksum`.

diskSizeGiB.description:
The clones' OS disk size, in GiB. `COS_PERSISTENT` fills a disk of
this size and does not grow on a larger one, and a smaller one cannot
hold the image: give the classes that use this image this disk size
(ADR-0113 Decision 4).

sources.description:
Per-provider source mappings — one backend binding for this catalog
entry per `providerClass` you intend to schedule VMs onto ("one
name, many backends", see the type-level doc comment above).

`x-kubernetes-list-type: map` keyed on `providerClass`: the API
server rejects a second entry for a `providerClass` that already
has one, rather than leaving it to `find_url_source` /
`find_vsphere_source` to silently pick whichever came first.

items.description:
One backend's mapping for a VMImage: which provider class it applies to,
and how to find (or import) the image there.

checksum.description:
Optional checksum for imported images. Format: `<alg>:<hex>`,
e.g. `sha256:9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b...`.
Supported algorithms: `sha256`, `sha512`. Provider import Jobs verify
the built artifact against this value before writing it to the backend
and fail closed on mismatch or an unsupported algorithm.

importFrom.description:
Optional source URL. When set, providers that support image import
will pull from here if the image isn't already present locally.

kind.description: What kind of backend artifact `ref` refers to.

providerClass.description:
Name of the ProviderClass this source applies to. Conventional
values: `vsphere`, `proxmox`, `libvirt`.

ref.description:
Provider-interpreted reference:
  vsphere + Template:     template name e.g. "ubuntu-22.04-cloudinit"
  proxmox + Template:     template VMID e.g. "9000"
  libvirt + BackingFile:  path e.g. "/var/lib/libvirt/images/ubuntu.qcow2"
  firecracker + OciArtifact: `<repository>@sha256:<manifest digest>`
  * + Url:                ignored; uses `importFrom`

template.description:
How the backend **template** is built from a `Url` source (root
folder, network, disk, CPU / memory / firmware / NIC, force knobs).
Every field is optional and falls back to a built-in default. Only
meaningful for `Url` sources, with one exception: for a vSphere
`Template` source (an existing template banlieue adopts and never
builds) only `rootFolder` is read, to find the template in
`<rootFolder>/<failure-domain>`; every other field is ignored.
Ignored for `BackingFile`. See `VMImageTemplate`, ADR-0020 and
ADR-0104.

cpus.description:
Virtual CPU count of the template (`govc vm.create -c`). When unset,
defaults to 2. vSphere-only.

disk.description:
Install disk of the template (the clone source's disk). When unset, a
thin 100 GiB disk on a pvscsi controller is used.

size.description: Disk size, in GiB. Defaults to 100 when unset.

type.description:
Provisioning hint: `thin` (default), `thick`, or `eagerZeroed`. Reuses
the backend-agnostic `DiskProvisioning` shared with `VMClass` /
`VSphereMachine`; eager-zeroing is the `eagerZeroed` variant, not a
separate flag. Providers honor it on a best-effort basis.

firmware.description:
Firmware for the template (`govc vm.create -firmware`). Reuses the
backend-agnostic `Firmware` hint (`bios` / `efi` / `efi-secure`). When
unset, defaults to `efi`. vSphere maps `efi-secure` to EFI with secure
boot enabled.

forceCreate.description:
Recreate the template even if one of that name already exists,
destroying the existing one first. Threaded as `--force-create`.

forceUpload.description:
Re-upload the built ISO even if one of that name already exists on the
backend, deleting the existing one first (the vСenter datastore file API
does not overwrite in place). Threaded as `--force-upload`.

guestId.description:
vCenter `guestId` for the template (`govc vm.create -g`, e.g.
`rhel9_64Guest`, `ubuntu64Guest`). When unset, it is derived from the
VMImage's `osFamily` / `osDistribution` / `osVersion`. vSphere-only.

installMode.description:
How the template's install step is driven. See `InstallMode` and
ADR-0021 / ADR-0040.

installTimeoutSeconds.description:
Bound, in seconds, on how long the import Job waits for the
unattended Kairos install to finish and the VM to power itself off
(`install.poweroff: true` in the cloud-config) before failing the
Job. When unset, defaults to 1800 (30 min). See ADR-0021: the golden
disk is never rebooted by the build, so this bounds only the
(typically 8-12 min) unattended-install window, not a boot cycle.

memoryMib.description:
Memory of the template, in MiB (`govc vm.create -m`). When unset,
defaults to 4096. vSphere-only.

network.description:
The template's network interfaces. Empty means exactly one NIC, using
every per-entry default below — the same behavior this field had
before it became a list (ADR-0031). vSphere-only.

items.description: One network interface on a `Url`-source template (ADR-0031).

adapter.description: Virtual NIC adapter type for the template (`govc vm.create -net.adapter`).

network.description:
Port group this NIC attaches to. When unset, the zone's first
reachable network class (ADR-0019) is used.

pciSlot.description:
PCI slot number for this NIC (`ethernetN.pciSlotNumber`). Slot 192
on the first NIC yields a stable `ens192` interface name in the
guest. When unset, defaults to `192 + this NIC's index` in
`VMImageTemplate.network` — so a template with several NICs and no
explicit slots still gets predictable, non-colliding
`ens192`/`ens193`/`ens194`/... naming.

retainOnDelete.description:
Keep the per-zone vCenter template(s) this `VMImage` caused to be
built when the `VMImage` itself is deleted. When unset (the default),
deleting a `VMImage` also destroys every per-zone template it owns —
declarative deletion, matching `VirtualMachine`'s own cascade onto its
`VSphereMachine` (ADR-0026). Set `true` to opt out — e.g. the template
is still referenced by another generation, or its lifecycle is
managed by hand outside banlieue. vSphere-only; ignored by any other
provider. See ADR-0028.

rootFolder.description:
Root vCenter inventory folder (path under the datacenter's VM folder,
e.g. `templates/kairos`); created if missing. When unset, the
datacenter's VM-folder root is the root. vSphere-only. Read for both
`Url` (where the template is created) and `Template` (where the
existing template is looked up) sources (ADR-0104).

Named `rootFolder`, not `folder`, because it is never the literal
target: the per-zone import always places the template at
`<rootFolder>/<failure-domain-name>` (ADR-0020). Two failure domains
commonly share a datacenter (only their cluster differs), and
vSphere's VM/Template folder hierarchy is scoped per-datacenter, not
per-cluster — without the per-zone subfolder, every zone's import
raced `CreateVM_Task` against the identical folder + template name.

trustedBoot.description:
Requests a Trusted Boot (UKI) artifact instead of a classic
kernel+initrd one, for `Url`-kind vSphere sources. Resolved by
`banlieue-imagebuilder` into the kairos-operator `OSArtifact`'s
`spec.artifacts.uki.{iso,keysVolume}` (replacing the plain
`artifacts.iso` request) — the `auroraboot build-uki` mechanism. See
`TrustedBootSource` and ADR-0051. Ignored for `cloudImage`-kind
builds and non-`Url` sources.

secretRef.description:
Secret in the imagebuild namespace holding the six files
`auroraboot build-uki` requires: `PK.auth`, `KEK.auth`, `db.auth`,
`db.key`, `db.pem`, `tpm2-pcr-private.pem`. Generated out-of-band via
`auroraboot genkey` — banlieue never generates or manages this key
material.

status.description:
Observed availability of a VMImage across the Providers that can serve it.
Maintained by the image controller; read by the scheduler.

buildArtifact.description:
Progress of the shared, provider-agnostic image build for `Url`-kind
sources — set exclusively by `banlieue-imagebuilder` (field manager
`banlieue.io/imagebuilder`), never by a provider. Typed by `kind`
(`cloudImage` for libvirt, `iso` for vSphere). `None` when no `Url`
source exists on this `VMImage` or the build hasn't started. See
ADR-0010 and ADR-0020.

checksum.description:
Expected checksum (`<alg>:<hex>`) of the built artifact, copied from the
`Url` source the build serves. Consumers that stream the artifact to a
backend MUST verify it against this value and fail closed on mismatch
(security review 2026-07-31, SEC-004) — the value lives here, next to
the PVC reference, so no consumer has to re-derive which source the
shared build came from.

file.description:
File name of the artifact within the artifacts PVC (kairos-operator
convention: `<osArtifactRef>.raw` for `cloudImage`, `<osArtifactRef>.iso`
for `iso`). Populated at phase `Ready`.

firstBootSealingLayer.description:
Whether this build carries the banlieue-generated first-boot sealing
layer (ADR-0088): set when `spec.firstBootSealing` was honoured by the
merged cloud-config this artifact was built from. Omitted when false.

kind.description:
What kind of artifact was built, aligned with kairos-operator's own
`OSArtifactKind`. Determines the `file` extension and which provider
class consumes it.

message.description:
Long human-readable detail, e.g. the `OSArtifact.status.message` on
failure.

ociArtifact.description:
The same artifact, pushed to an OCI registry for providers that run
outside the cluster and cannot mount the artifacts PVC (ADR-0064).
Set only when a `cloud-hypervisor` `Url` source exists; `None`
otherwise, so installs without a host-resident provider need no
registry.

message.description: Human-readable detail, e.g. why the push failed.

reference.description:
Digest-pinned reference, `registry/repository@sha256:<hex>`, once the
push succeeded. Consumers pull **by this digest** and nothing else:
integrity comes from content addressing, so a tag moved after the
push cannot change what a host boots.

osArtifactRef.description:
Name of the `OSArtifact` CR `banlieue-imagebuilder` created for this
`VMImage` (same namespace as the artifacts PVC below).

osArtifactUid.description:
`metadata.uid` of the `OSArtifact` named by `os_artifact_ref`, once
observed. Each provider's per-zone import Job sets this as its own
`ownerReference` so a rebuilt (deleted-and-recreated) `OSArtifact`
garbage-collects the stale Job — and the artifacts PVC mount it
holds — instead of the Job outliving it for up to its
`ttlSecondsAfterFinished` (ADR-0027). Absent until the `OSArtifact`
has actually been observed once.

prelaidDiskSizeGiB.description:
The disk size, in GiB, the artifact was pre-laid for (ADR-0113), when
`spec.prelay` was honoured: `file` is then the pre-laid image and
`checksum` its digest, computed by the builder. Omitted otherwise.

pvcRef.description:
Reference to the PVC kairos-operator created holding the built artifact,
once known. Populated no earlier than phase `Building`.

reason.description:
Short reason, mirroring the stable-string convention used elsewhere
in this status (e.g. `ImagePerProviderStatus.reason`).

conditions.description:
`Ready` is True iff every per-provider entry is ready.

Written **only** by `banlieue-controller` (field manager
`banlieue.io/controller`), which is the only component with a
whole-image view. A provider cannot compute "ready everywhere" from
rows it does not own, so it writes its `perProvider` entry and nothing
here (ADR-0015). Merge-keyed on `type`, per Kubernetes convention.

items.description: Condition contains details for one aspect of the current state of this API Resource.

lastTransitionTime.description: lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.

message.description: message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string.

observedGeneration.description: observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance.

reason.description: reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty.

status.description: status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.

type.description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.

firstBootSealing.description: How banlieue knows an image seals itself on first boot (ADR-0088).

perProvider.description:
Per-Provider readiness. One entry per Provider that supports this
image's providerClass and has reconciled at least once.

**Merge-keyed, and it must stay that way (ADR-0015).** Several
providers write this list concurrently, each applying only its own
entry. Without `x-kubernetes-list-type: map` server-side apply treats
the array as atomic — one manager owns the whole thing and `force()`
hands it over wholesale, silently discarding every other provider's
row. That was a real, reproduced bug, not a theoretical one.

items.description: Readiness of a VMImage on one specific Provider.

ready.description: True when the image can be used to clone/create a VM on this provider.

reason.description:
Short reason if not ready. Stable values from
`condition_reasons::IMAGE_*`.

resolvedRef.description:
Resolved concrete reference on the backend, for backends with one
reference per provider. Proxmox: VMID. Libvirt: path. Unset for
vSphere, whose per-zone references are in `Self::zones` (ADR-0104).

zones.description:
Per-zone (per-`Provider.status.failureDomains[]`) readiness. Populated
by the vSphere provider for both `Url` sources (import progress) and
`Template` sources (whether the adopted template exists in each zone's
folder, ADR-0104). For `Url`, `ready` means every zone is ready; for
`Template` it means at least one zone is, and the scheduler places
VMs only in ready zones. Empty for backends without zones (libvirt,
Proxmox).

items.description:
Readiness of a `VMImage` in one failure domain (zone) of a Provider. For
`Url`-kind sources, built by `banlieue-imagebuilder` and imported per zone
by the owning provider's controller (e.g. `banlieue-provider-vsphere`, one
zone == one vSphere compute cluster / datastore / network in the current
environment), it is import progress (ADR-0010). For vSphere `Template`
sources it is whether the adopted template exists in this zone's folder
(ADR-0104).

name.description: Name of the failure domain, matching `Provider.status.failureDomains[].name`.

ready.description:
True once the template is usable in this zone (import finished for
`Url`; template found in the zone's folder for `Template`).

resolvedRef.description:
The template's bare display name within this zone once ready — the
value a provider passes to a name-based template lookup. NOT a
decorated string (no `[dc]`/folder prefix): the folder lives in
`Self::template_folder`, kept separate so a lookup can be built
from structured fields instead of parsing this one.

templateFolder.description:
The vCenter folder path (relative to the datacenter's VM folder,
e.g. `templates/cluster-01`) the template in `Self::resolved_ref`
lives in: `<spec.template.rootFolder>/<zone>` for both `Url` imports
(ADR-0020 Decision #5) and `Template` sources (ADR-0104). Unset while
the zone is not ready.
